thesis: The single most valuable conversion mechanism on this site is the coverage-check CTA, which is the primary entry point for visitors to determine if the service is available at their address. This mechanism is bleeding value due to inconsistent CTA labels across the site, causing ambiguity and friction, and the site's severe performance issues (LCP of 50.8s) that cause most visitors to bounce before they can even interact with the CTA.

findings.title: Lab LCP 50.8s mobile
findings.summary: Lab Largest Contentful Paint of 50.8 seconds on mobile causes most visitors to bounce before seeing content.
findings.problem: Lab Largest Contentful Paint of 50.8 seconds on mobile causes most visitors to bounce before seeing content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse (mobile emulation, single synthetic run via DataForSEO): Largest Contentful Paint 50.8 s against a ‘good’ threshold of 2500ms. Lab data, not real-user field data — confirms the defect class, not the field percentile.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 2.0-8.0% relative lift

findings.title: Conflicting coverage CTAs
findings.summary: Multiple different CTA labels for the same coverage-check action create ambiguity about the next step.
findings.problem: Multiple different CTA labels for the same coverage-check action create ambiguity about the next step.
findings.recommended_change: h1: Reliable Internet That Works Anywhere in the U.S.; cta: Single consistent CTA label, e.g., 'Check Coverage'; notes: Consolidate all coverage-check CTAs into one consistent label and action.
findings.evidence: CHECK COVERAGE | CHECK IF IT WORKS AT MY ADDRESS | SEE MY OPTIONS | SEE WHAT I QUALIFY FOR | CHECK MY COVERAGE
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Headline omits unlimited promise
findings.summary: The primary headline fails to mention the unlimited data benefit, leaving a key differentiator unstated above the fold.
findings.problem: The primary headline fails to mention the unlimited data benefit, leaving a key differentiator unstated above the fold.
findings.recommended_change: h1: Reliable Internet That Works Anywhere in the U.S. with Unlimited Data; notes: Add 'unlimited' to headline or hero subcopy.
findings.evidence: The page's main headline reads “Reliable Internet That Works Anywhere in the U.S”. | Message_match: promises_missing_from_headline: ["unlimited"]
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Lab TBT 3500ms mobile
findings.summary: Lab Total Blocking Time of 3,500 ms on mobile freezes the main thread, making the page unresponsive during load.
findings.problem: Lab Total Blocking Time of 3,500 ms on mobile freezes the main thread, making the page unresponsive during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse (mobile emulation, single synthetic run via DataForSEO): Total Blocking Time 3,500 ms against a ‘good’ threshold of 200ms. Lab data, not real-user field data — confirms the defect class, not the field percentile.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Lab CLS 0.265 mobile
findings.summary: Lab Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.265 on mobile causes layout jumps, leading to mis-taps on critical buttons.
findings.problem: Lab Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.265 on mobile causes layout jumps, leading to mis-taps on critical buttons.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse (mobile emulation, single synthetic run via DataForSEO): Cumulative Layout Shift 0.265 against a ‘good’ threshold of 0.1. Lab data, not real-user field data — confirms the defect class, not the field percentile.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Unlabeled form fields
findings.summary: Form fields lack visible labels, so visitors cannot tell what information is required before submitting.
findings.problem: Form fields lack visible labels, so visitors cannot tell what information is required before submitting.
findings.recommended_change: notes: Add visible, persistent labels above each input.
findings.evidence: Form fields on coverage and qualification forms have no visible labels.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Inconsistent price formatting
findings.summary: The same plans display conflicting price formats and values across pages, undermining trust in cost clarity.
findings.problem: The same plans display conflicting price formats and values across pages, undermining trust in cost clarity.
findings.recommended_change: notes: Standardize all price displays to a single format, e.g., $99.95/month, and remove or label $0.00 values.
findings.evidence: Prices shown on the page: $99.95/month $129.95/month $99.95/Mo $99.95/month $129.95/month $99.95 | Prices shown on the page: $99.95/month $129.95/month $99.95/mo $0.00 $99.95 $99.99 | A section heading reads “$0.00 (one-time)”.
findings.analysts_agreeing: Pricing & Cost Transparency, Navigation & Information Scent
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Duplicate form submissions
findings.summary: Two identical CONTINUE forms on the same page create competing submission points and confusion.
findings.problem: Two identical CONTINUE forms on the same page create competing submission points and confusion.
findings.recommended_change: h1: Reliable Internet That Works Anywhere in the U.S.; cta: Single CONTINUE form; notes: Remove duplicate form to leave one clear submission path.
findings.evidence: Two identical CONTINUE forms appear on the same page.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 0.5-2.0% relative lift

findings.title: Value prop buried under questions
findings.summary: The hero area leads with qualification questions instead of stating the product's value, delaying message clarity.
findings.problem: The hero area leads with qualification questions instead of stating the product's value, delaying message clarity.
findings.recommended_change: h1: High-Speed Wireless Internet for Anywhere You Live or Travel; notes: Move questions below a concise value statement.
findings.evidence: The page's main headline reads “Let's Get You the Right Internet”. | The page's main headline reads “What Best Describes Your Time on the Road?”. | The page's main headline reads “How Do You Use the Internet at Home?”.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 0.5-2.0% relative lift

findings.title: Duplicate H1s dilute focus
findings.summary: Multiple H1 headings on the same page fragment the primary message and weaken information scent.
findings.problem: Multiple H1 headings on the same page fragment the primary message and weaken information scent.
findings.recommended_change: h1: Single H1 matching visitor intent; notes: Keep one H1 per page and demote others to H2s.
findings.evidence: The page's main headline reads “Reliable Internet That Works Anywhere in the U.S”. | The page's main headline reads “Internet That Just Works”. | The page's main headline reads “Let's Get You the Right Internet”.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 0.5-2.0% relative lift
